articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as C.E.O.
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as C.E.O.
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday morning that he spoke directly to Nvidia 's board and urged them to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang .
"I spoke to them, let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview shortly after Nvidia's shock announcement that Huang was returning to lead the tech giant.
"And I convinced them," the president said. "I made the deal."
Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang came less than two weeks after he resigned. Huang had stepped down after admitting he cheated on his wife and amid claims his affairs included one with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees.
Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, Alice Huang, and her role as an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed raised concerns that she was facilitating the diversion of  Nvidia's most advanced semiconductor chip to China.
Trump said Nvidia's board "did ask for assurance on the national security threat," Trump said.
"And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot," the president said.
Trump said that after he spoke with Nvidia's board, "when the deal was finished," he called Huang.
"I called him up, and I said: 'I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,'" Trump said.
"I didn't talk about other things because he understands that. He understands it better than we do," the president said. "He knows what to do and what not to do. But I just said work hard because if you work hard, there's nobody that can capture what you've done. Nobody, nobody close."
Trump also told CNBC that Huang "did nothing wrong."
"I think the [Nvidia] board acted really responsibly" in deciding to bring Huang back.
"People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it's a threat to lose him," the president said.
"I'm very, very happy that the company had the courage and the board had the courage to do the right thing, and they suffered for two weeks, and the company suffered greatly," the president said.
Asked whether the broad stock market selloff last week after Huang's resignation from Nvidia factored into his decision to push for the CEO's reinstatement, Trump said, "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term."
"The bigger impact was, you know, he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about," Trump said.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang went to war with Washington — and won a path to China
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang went to war with Washington — and won a path to China
articles.content_orig:
Huang had resigned over an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.
President Donald Trump is taking credit for Jensen Huang's stunning return to Nvidia , saying in an interview on Monday that he spoke "directly and indirectly" to the company's board members about bringing Huang back as CEO.
The surprise move comes just days after Huang, who was accused of having an affair with a person alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset, offered to rejoin the company and Nvidia said it did not intend to reinstate him .
"I spoke to them. Let me put it this way: And I convinced them. I made the deal," Trump, who had urged Huang's reinstatement publicly, said in a phone interview with CNBC .
The president called the decision by the Nvidia board to reinstate Huang as CEO and president "very exciting news."
"We have to protect our geniuses, and he's certainly a genius," Trump said.
Trump said a "very thorough investigation" by the U.S. government "exonerated" Huang and determined that he "did nothing wrong."
ABC News has reached out to the White House for clarification on which investigation Trump was referring to in the CNBC interview.

NBC Selected independently determines what we cover and recommend. When you click on or buy through our links, we earn a commission. Learn more .
The countdown is officially here: there are only four days until Black Friday 2026 . That doesn’t mean you should wait to shop, however. Amazon , Walmart , Home Depot , Apple , PlayStation , Alo , Hoka , Nintendo and more already rolled out deals, and at this point, once a product’s price drops, you can be pretty confident that it’s the best offer you’ll see.
I’ve spent over six years covering major sales as a reporter and on-air correspondent for NBC Selected. I’ve been tracking prices for weeks and combing through thousands of discounts to find the best Black Friday deals actually worth buying . Each one I recommend below is highly rated and 20 percent off or more. When possible, I also ran deals through price trackers like CamelCamelCamel to make sure they’re at their lowest price in at least three months — I even found seven that are currently at their lowest price ever. I’m updating this live today, November 23, with my expert-approved picks, so save this link and check back in often.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
I use my AirPods Pro 3 every day to listen to music, take calls and watch TV. I’m always impressed by how much noise they block while I’m commuting or at the gym, and I appreciate the ability to use transparency mode when I want to be aware of my surroundings. The earbuds also have built-in heart rate sensing, live language translation, hearing aid and hearing test features. They come with five sets of ear tips in different sizes, which lets you customize their fit, and a charging case that extends their battery life.
Hoka ’s Arahi sneakers are one of our favorite pairs, and since the brand recently released the ninth edition, the previous one is currently on sale. Hoka made minimal changes between the models, so it’s worth buying the Arahi 8 if you need a solid walking or running shoe . It has a built-in stability system that helps prevent overpronation, and a moderate layer of soft cushioning to absorb shock and keep your feet comfortable. The sneakers come in regular and wide styles, and men’s and women’s sizes.
Batteries are an essential you always need to have at home, so you may as well buy them on sale, especially before the holidays — in my family, they’re always in high demand to power remotes, lights and toys. This pack comes with 48 total: 24 AA and 24 AAA . The batteries hold their power for up to 10 years in storage and they’re leak-resistant for up to two years, according to the brand.
The most life-changing product I’ve used in 2026 is a robot vacuum and mop like this one. It picks up dirt, hair and crumbs while scrubbing floors to leave them sparkling — and the best part is that you don’t have to lift a finger. When the robot is done cleaning, it returns to its charging base and empties itself into the dustbag. It maps your home to detect where carpets, hard floors and obstacles are, and connects to an app that lets you set schedules and routines, as well as adjust settings.
It’s almost time to get out your holiday pajama set , and Gap is discounting a handful of styles to help you refresh your collection. This one comes with a long sleeve shirt and long pants, both of which are made from 100% cotton. The set has a relaxed fit that won’t restrict you while sleeping, lounging or running errands. It comes in five festive prints, and there are matching options for men , kids , babies and toddlers .
You’ll always find at least one person wearing these retro over-ear headphones at NBC Selected’s office. You can choose from four noise-cancellation levels depending on how well you want to hear the world around you, and take calls while wearing them thanks to built-in microphones. The headphones have multiple buttons on them that let you adjust the volume, shuffle through tracks and engage a voice assistant, as well as control your connected device’s camera. A full battery gives you up to 135 hours of battery life, according to the brand.
The spherical shape of Wonderboom’s portable Bluetooth speaker gives you 360-degree sound, and a full battery lasts for up to 14 hours, according to the brand. It also floats and is water-resistant, so you can use it in the pool, at the beach or while taking a bath. The speaker has outdoor boost and podcast modes to enhance audio as needed, and there’s a loop on the top, which you can add a carabiner clip to and attach it to your bag, bike or lounge chair.
If you’re not a smartwatch person but want to track health metrics, try the Oura Ring 5 , which is the brand’s smallest, most low-profile device yet. It has sensors on the inside that detect your pulse, letting it collect insights about your sleep, workouts, heart rate, stress levels and more. All the data it collects gets stored in the Oura app, where you also get a daily readiness score. The Oura Ring is water- and scratch-resistant, and a full battery lasts for about a week. Note: a $5.99 per month Oura membership , sold separately, is required for use, but you get a one-month membership free with your purchase.
Get rid of dirt, crumbs, hair and dust with Shark’s vacuum , which has a built-in HEPA that traps grime inside. You can quickly turn the brushroll on and off depending on what type of floors you’re cleaning, and detach the pod to tackle hard to reach areas like stairs and furniture. The pod has a long hose and you interchangeable attachments: a dusting brush and a crevice tool.
Ryobi’s drill and driver kit helps you get home improvement projects done fast and efficiently. It includes one 18-volt ½-inch drill/driver and one 18-volt ¼-inch impact driver, plus a charger and storage bag. The drill/driver delivers up to 515 pounds of torque, while the impact driver delivers up to 1,800 pounds of torque. Both tools have built-in LED lights to help you see your workspace clearly.
Legos are one of the best holiday gifts for collectors and anyone who enjoys hands-on activities. This set comes with all the pieces you or your giftee needs to construct a red fox, which has a movable head, neck, legs, mouth, paws and tail when it’s done. It comes with a snow-covered tree stump and spruce tree stand, letting you display the fox in its habitat. The red fox is moderately challenging and best for those 9 years old and up.
As someone who’s owned a Stanley Quencher for at least four years, I can say with certainty that it withstands the test of time. Mine is just as durable as ever, and it continues to keep my drinks cold and ice frozen for hours thanks to its stainless steel construction and double-walled vacuum insulation. The water bottle’s narrow base is cup holder-friendly, and it has a lid you can move into three different positions: straw opening, drink opening and full-cover top. There’s also a large handle that makes it comfortable to hold.
You’ll be an at-home barista in no time with De’Longhi’s Classic Signature Espresso Machine , which also has a built-in adjustable steam wand to froth or steam milk. You can brew single or double shots of espresso hot or over ice, and customize preset recipes to make your coffee routine as simple as possible. The machine has a large 57-ounce water tank and an adjustable drip tray, too.
If you order these oven mitts now, they might arrive before Thanksgiving to help you move hot pots and pans around your kitchen. They’re covered in a water-resistant ribbed silicone material that lets you securely grip cookware, and they’re heat-resistant up to 500 degrees Fahrenheit. The inside of the mitts have a soft cotton cuff with polyester lining, which adds an extra layer of protection from high temperatures. There’s a loop on the end of the oven mitts that let you hang them up.

articles.title_orig: A ‘GTA 6’ Player Finds Tommy Vercetti’s Shirt And Portal To Original Vice City
articles.title_zh: A ‘GTA 6’ Player Finds Tommy Vercetti’s Shirt And Portal To Original Vice City
articles.content_orig:
Join 100K+ fans and never miss breaking news, fan theories, trailers and exclusive content.
Rockstar Games has always been known for hiding complex secrets across its open worlds, but GTA 6 has already delivered one of the most ambitious nostalgia trips in the franchise’s story. Just days after its launch, an Instagram user @memeio.yt has found a way back to enter the classic 2002 GTA Vice City map.
A post shared by Memeio (@memeio.yt)
According to the player, the portal to cross in-game dimensions is locked behind a puzzle that has something to do with Leonida Power & Light (LPL), the electric utility company operating in the gorgeous state of Leonida . The puzzle spans several locations, but the reward you get after completing it will win you over.
Cracked by @memeio.yt after three days of tracking clues across Leonida’s power grid, the Easter Egg doesn’t settle for a simple visual nod. Stepping through the hidden portal shifts GTA 6 into a PlayStation 2 visual style, dropping players inside a faithful 1980s recreation of the Malibu Club. Waiting inside is none other than Kent Paul, with actor Danny Dyer reprising his role for the surprise cameo. This makes him one of the most shocking returning characters in GTA 6 .
Once the throwback sequence wraps up and players return to modern-day Leonida, they keep two permanent rewards:
What makes the discovery even more impressive is how Rockstar built the map-spanning puzzle. The secret revolves around 12 LPL power stations scattered across Leonida. Each of these stations is marked with painted letters that spell out “LIFE IS PASSING ME BY” – the classic GTA Vice City cheat code that speeds up the in-game time.
At each station, buttons and levers are taped with W, A, D, or . (a single dot) , mirroring the layout of a PlayStation 2 controller. Here’s how:
Hitting the right switch at each stop recreates the exact PS2 button combo for the original cheat code: Circle, Circle, L1, Square, L1, Square, Square, Square, L1, Triangle, Circle, Triangle . This is just genius by Rockstar!
For those who want to revisit 2002 GTA Vice City in GTA 6 and claim Tommy Vercetti’s outfit and bike, here’s a detailed guide for you. But before that, there are a few things that you must note:
Head over to the Badger Radio Tower in Key Lento and climb upstairs into the control room. It is at the very top of the tower. Inside, you will find a lever, a button, and a poster of a PlayStation controller reading “Lost Track of Time.” Interact with the lever and press the button to trigger the GTA Vice City portal puzzle in GTA 6 . A brief flash of the Malibu Club and a familiar sound effect (from Vice City ) will confirm the quest is active.
Now comes the most important part – visiting each of the 12 LPL substations across Leonida without fast traveling and pressing the right buttons. For your reference, we have mentioned the correct order of substations and buttons to solve this puzzle quickly:
Immediately after pulling the final W lever at substation 12, you will receive a text from an unknown number saying “U-235 REACTOR 19-06.” The text is basically asking you to go to Reactor 2 between 7:00 PM and 6:00 AM. That being said, head over to LPL Turtle Head Power Station, wait until the in-game clock passes 7:00 PM, and walk into Reactor 2.
After that, a glowing portal will appear near the reactor. You can head over to the portal and pull a lever. Doing so will teleport you to PS2-style 2002 GTA Vice City ‘s Malibu Club. There, you can dance with other NPCs and buy yourself a nice drink at the bar counter.
There’s a hidden staircase on the left side of the bar counter that will lead you to Kent Paul. After a brief interaction with him, another portal will appear that will take you back to the GTA 6 world. However, you will spawn with Tommy Vercetti’s shirt and his bike. Both of these are permanent rewards, so you don’t have to worry about losing them.
The only thing you need to worry about is not pressing the wrong button during the entire mission. Also, worry about your in-game wallet if you haven’t robbed the best loot spots in GTA 6 yet! We have a dedicated guide on that.
Anyway, did you like this Easter Egg? Or will you still vote for Dexter’s apartment ? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya
articles.title_zh: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya
articles.content_orig:
In this satellite image provided by Vantor, the capsized Russian navy corvette Merkury is seen following a suspected drone strike, at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/via AP hide caption
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.
Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made sea drones in the operation, which struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 invasion of its neighbor, the Ukrainian leader said in a post on X.
Russian officials made no immediate comment.
The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.
In this screen grab from a video provided by the Security Service of Ukraine on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, a Ukrainian Sea Baby suicide drone attacks the Russian navy corvette Merkury near Benghazi, Libya. Security Service of Ukraine/via AP hide caption
Ukraine has at times blindsided Russia during the war with ingenious attacks that embarrass Moscow, such as Operation Spiderweb in June last year, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked near air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's cutting-edge drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army.
At the same time, Russia's strategic bombing of Ukraine has devastated the power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings.
A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said Monday. A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled from the rubble after the Sunday morning attack, rescue services said.
Zelenskyy described Sunday's attack as "exemplary" and said "the targets we set were achieved."
"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said.
In this screen grab from a video provided by the Security Service of Ukraine on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, a Ukrainian Sea Baby suicide drone attacks the Russian navy corvette Merkury near Benghazi, Libya. Security Service of Ukraine/via AP hide caption
Ukraine has hit Russian oil refineries as far away as western Siberia and Russian warships in the Mediterranean, Zelenskyy noted in a live video address Monday to a meeting of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.
"We keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack," Zelenskyy said.
Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons, and destroyed a Ka-27 military helicopter in the attack, the Ukrainian leader said.
Ukrainian forces are operating in western Libya under a covert deal endorsed by the West, using the North African country's territory to strike a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in March, according to Libyan officials.
The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, were at the time operating mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also in other military facilities in the capital Tripoli and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press earlier this year.
Sunday's attack severely damaged the Russian corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya, according to two Libyan officials.
Residents in Benghazi heard loud explosions and saw flames at the base early Sunday. Civil defense units rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said.
The vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies as part of a cooperation agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, a statement said without providing details about the vessel or its cargo.
The government in eastern Libya sent a letter to U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres and the U.N. Security Council, calling for an international investigation into the potential use of western Libya to prepare and launch Sunday's attack.
Libyan officials who were briefed on the attack told The Associated Press that at least four drones were intercepted while two hit the corvette, which is designed to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.
At least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded in the attack, one of the officials said.
In this screen grab from a video provided by the Security Service of Ukraine on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, a Ukrainian Sea Baby suicide drone attacks the Russian navy corvette Merkury near Benghazi, Libya. Security Service of Ukraine/via AP hide caption
The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.
Ambrey, a U.K.-based maritime security and risk intelligence firm, said that some of the explosions at the Benghazi Naval Base were likely caused by the detonation of ammunition on board the Russian warship.
Hours after the warship attack, another sea drone strike hit a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel sailing off Benghazi, the Libyan coast guard said.
Ukraine's Security Service, or SBU, described the operation as "unique." It said the cargo ship MV Angara was sanctioned and used to transport Russian military equipment, and the multipurpose corvette Merkury regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including guarding the MV Angara.
The drones were delivered to a designated location and launched from a so-called "mothership" near the target, the SBU said.
A Ka-27 helicopter was on board the corvette and also went under, the SBU added.
Russian defenses tried from air, sea and land to hit the attacking drones, it said.
"Ukraine's defense forces have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea," which borders both Russia and Ukraine, the SBU said.

articles.title_orig: For Netanyahu, losing power could mean losing key shield in corruption trial
articles.title_zh: For Netanyahu, losing power could mean losing key shield in corruption trial
articles.content_orig:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his family will likely be questioned over corruption allegations sometime later this month, Israeli media reported Thursday.
According to the Times of Israel news website, Israeli police have asked the attorney-general for permission to question Netanyahu and his wife Sara -- and, possibly, his son Yair -- before the Jewish Passover holiday, which will begin March 30.
The expected questioning comes within the context of an ongoing corruption probe involving the Bezeq telecommunication company.
The case involves accusations that Bezeq owner Shaul Elovitch had instructed the Walla news website, which he owns, to provide Netanyahu with positive media coverage.
Last month, Israeli police recommended that Netanyahu be indicted for alleged corruption, saying there was now sufficient evidence to formally charge him in two separate graft cases.
The first case involves Israeli Hollywood producer Arnon Milchan, who was allegedly asked to purchase luxury items for Netanyahu and his wife.
The second relates to an alleged deal -- again for favorable media coverage -- with Arnon Mozes, publisher of Hebrew-language daily Yedioth Ahronoth.

Samsung is working on a new look for the Now Bar's live notifications, and the resemblance to Apple's Dynamic Island is hard to miss. We've exclusively discovered the changes in early Galaxy S27 series software, offering a glimpse of how Samsung could present ongoing activities in a future update.
On current versions of One UI, the live notification pill sits beside the clock on the left. Samsung's new layout moves it to the top center, in the area around the front camera.
The timer countdown, Torch indicator, and expandable activity controls you see here are familiar features already in One UI. The new layout displays those existing updates from this central position.
Centered torch Now Bar pill
Centered timer Now Bar pill
Samsung is also changing how you switch between compact live notification pills. Currently, you swipe up and down to move between ongoing activities. In the version we tested, you swipe left and right instead, without first expanding the pill.
That sideways switching gesture, combined with the placement around the selfie camera, gives Samsung's existing live notifications a more Dynamic Island-like feel.
Now Bar settings also include a Moment effects page, with Sports as the only listed download. It offers celebrations for your favorite teams' scores and wins in selected sports supported by Google Sports.
Samsung has already introduced sports animations in the One UI 9.5 beta . The broader Moment effects name could leave room for other types of effects later, but additional categories haven't been confirmed.
All of these changes are still under development and could be revised before Samsung brings them to Galaxy devices. They will likely debut with the Galaxy S27 series before reaching existing devices through the One UI 9.5 update .

The firm said shared security data could support a unified investigation and response process that neither company currently offers independently. articles.content_orig:

Jensen Huang is returning to lead Nvidia after he left in the wake of a run of scandals , the company has said.
Mr Huang resigned from the company he helped found on 12 November, after reports of a number of affairs, including with one woman accused of being a Chinese spy. In the time since, Donald Trump and many tech leaders called for his return and a petition supporting him gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures – leading Mr Huang to report that he would return to the company if its board asked him to.
Now, Nvidia says that its board has unanimously agreed that he should return. The decision followed “a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang”, which left it satisfied with his “candour and ability to lead”, the board said.
Nvidia’s announcement came after a pressure campaign from people including Donald Trump, who had said hours before the announcement that re-hiring Mr Huang would be “the best thing for the company, and also, for the USA”. The two are close, and the president has repeatedly backed Mr Huang throughout the scandal.
In a Truth Social post immediately after Nvidia announced the decision to re-appoint Mr Huang, Trump said it was “the correct and proper decision”. “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” he wrote.
“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” the post continued, citing attorney general Todd Blanche’s statements that the government “does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct”. “On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump wrote.
In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said it had received “input from senior levels of the United States government” that had led it to be “confident” that Mr Huang does not pose a national security risk, it said. Critics had argued that Mr Huang’s relationship with an accused Chinese spy could undermine the US’s work to keep its chips, which are central to today’s AI technology, could be acquired by China .
“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C Jones, its chair. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company.”
Mr Huang said he was “honoured” to return to Nvidia. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said in a statement.
Nvidia had previously announced that it had launched an independent investigation into accusations that Mr Huang had been successfully targeted by a “foreign intelligence effort”. That will continue to its conclusion and Mr Huang is committed to co-operate with it, Nvidia said.
It has also recently formed a new committee that will oversee Nvidia’s compliance with trade rules and national security risks. Nvidia will appoint a new chief compliance officer who will oversee that work, it said, and it committed to co-operate with ongoing government investigations.
Those investigations are examining a host of allegations that have dogged Nvidia for some time, and became more widely discussed in the wake of the scandal and Mr Huang’s departure. Multiple investigations of the company ​are ⁠underway, including by the US SEC and the Department of Justice , related to everything from potential accounting issues to alleged chip smuggling.
After Mr Huang resigned, on 12 November, Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer Colette Kriss to run the company. But that decision was met with immediate criticism, and reports that Mr Huang did not have confidence in her as his successor.
In the days that followed, pressure had mounted on Nvidia’s board to re-appoint Mr Huang. Trump repeatedly backed his return, alongside other tech leaders such as Elon Musk , and a petition supporting him now has more than 200,000 signatures, including people claiming to be employees of and investors in Nvidia.
Last week, five days after his departure, Mr Huang posted his first public statement on the scandal. He said that he had seen “an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO” and that he would be “honoured” to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of the company and the country.
In the days that followed, Nvidia repeatedly denied that it was looking to bring him back. In its quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, for instance, Ms Kress said that it was “business as usual” and Mr Jones, the chair of its board, confirmed that Nvidia was not considering bringing back Mr Huang.
But Nvidia’s share price continued to fall, and has dropped more than 20 per cent since those earnings were announced. That provoked fears that concern about Nvidia and its falling share price could undermine the investment in the US’s AI industry, which in turn could have dramatic effects on the US economy.
In the wake of Mr Huang’s reinstatement, however, the company’s share price jumped back up. Nvidia’s share price was up 31 per cent in the moments after the announcement.

A tech snafu at one of the world’s busiest airports on Sunday is delaying thousands of Delta Airlines flights headed ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
An issue with Delta Airlines’ weight and balance system at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is responsible for the delay at one of the busiest airports in the country, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement posted on social media.
More than 3,550 flights traveling within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed as of Sunday afternoon, according to Flight Aware .
The governmental agency urged travelers to check in with the airline for the latest information on their flights, and said that steps have already been taken to fix the issue.
“Delta is working to resolve issues with the airline’s weight and balance automation system,” the FAA statement said. “These delays are not related to any FAA air traffic systems.”
Delta said it is working limit congestion at its Atlanta hub.
“Delta teams are using manual workarounds to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” said Delta spokesperson Natalie Duggan. “We thank our customers for their patience and our people for their professionalism."
The issue on Sunday comes after a communications failure grounded all flights nationwide earlier this month, leading New York Gov. Kathy Hochul to call for the removal of U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
Other recent technological malfunctions have impacted other industries, including online banking systems and Microsoft Outlook.
Delta Airlines did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Gothamist.

Published Nov 23, 2026 at 5:00 a.m. ET

Citi Bike members will soon pay less for electric bike rides under a new agreement between Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration and Lyft, which operates the bike-share program.
The deal will also freeze annual membership prices and other fees for members through May 2029.
Starting Jan. 19, 2027, Citi Bike members will pay no more than $3.65 for an e-bike ride lasting up to 45 minutes. The cap also applies to reduced-fare members and shorter rides that already cost less will remain at their current price.
Annual membership prices, member per-minute e-bike fees and charges for rides that exceed 45 minutes will be frozen at current rates until May 26, 2029, when Lyft’s contract with the city expires.
“Getting around New York City shouldn't come with a price tag that keeps climbing by the minute,” Mamdani wrote in a release announcing the agreement. “Because a more affordable city is one where getting around it doesn’t break the bank.”
Citi Bike members currently pay 27 cents per minute for e-bike rides, or $12.15 for a 45-minute ride, except for rides entering or leaving Manhattan, which are capped at $5.40. The annual membership fee is $239 and rides on regular bikes lasting up to 45 minutes are included.
Under the new agreement, members could save as much as $8.50 on a single e-bike ride, according to City Hall. The new cap replaces the existing $5.40 cap for rides entering or leaving Manhattan, as well as a one-time allotment of 60 e-bike minutes for members.
The agreement doesn't prohibit Lyft from increasing Citi Bike prices for non-members, who currently pay $4.99 for a ride up to 30 minutes on analog bikes and an additional 41 cents per-minute for e-bike rides.
The city has also agreed to help install electric charging infrastructure at more than 130 Citi Bike stations starting next year. This will allow the e-bikes to recharge while docked, rather than having Lyft workers swap out depleted batteries. City officials said the changes will reduce operating costs and make more e-bikes available to riders.
City Councilmember Lincoln Restler introduced a bill two years ago to rein in the rising cost of Citi Bike rides.
“ This is such a tremendous victory for Citi Bike riders,” Restler said. “The city had given Lyft a monopoly, essentially, with the Citi Bike program and the cost spiraled out of control in such a way where it felt like New Yorkers were being taken advantage of.”
Citi Bike raised prices six times from 2022 through January 2026, with Lyft recently blaming tariffs and inflation for the need to raise rates.
“We’re grateful to Mayor Mamdani and Commissioner Flynn for working with us to make Citi Bike an even more sustainable, reliable, and affordable option for New Yorkers,” Patrick Knoth, general manager of Citi Bike, wrote in a statement.

Oil Slides Nearly 4% as Returning Supply Outweighs Gulf Attacks
The wider oil market remains…
Brent crude has broken back…
A market tipping point could…
Alex Kimani is a veteran finance writer, investor, engineer and researcher for Safehaven.com.
Oil prices have traded in a narrow range over the past few sessions as forecasts of a coming surplus collide with continued attacks and stalled diplomacy in the Middle East. A run of agency reports this month has pushed expectations toward oversupply and weighed on crude. Brent crude was up 1.1% at $92.88 per barrel at 11:50 a.m. ET on Thursday, well below its October levels above 110 dollars but little changed from the start of the week, while WTI crude gained 1.7% to 84.69 dollars per barrel. The International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its November Oil Market Report that the global oil market will return to surplus in the fourth quarter as Gulf exports recover faster than global demand. Global oil supply rose to 105.4 million barrels per day in October, and the agency now sees supply exceeding demand by 1.7 million bpd in Q4 2026, a swing from its previous forecast of a 1.8 million bpd deficit. The IEA raised its Q4 supply estimate by 3.3 million bpd from last month, cut its 2027 demand forecast by 80,000 bpd to 104.3 million bpd, and lowered the implied call on OPEC crude by 220,000 bpd to 20.8 million bpd.
The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) has moved in the same direction . In October, it forecast a 700,000 bpd inventory draw in the fourth quarter. It now expects stocks to build in Q4 and to rise by an average of 3.5 million bpd in the first half of 2027, after drawing down for most of this year. The EIA estimates that crude production shut in across the Gulf fell to 2.5 million bpd in October, from 4.8 million bpd in September and a peak of 10.9 million bpd in May. OPEC said crude output from the OPEC+ alliance rose by roughly 2 million bpd in October, led by Saudi Arabia and Iraq.
Related: Thanksgiving Gas Prices Could Break a Record Despite Recent Plunge
Analysts at Standard Chartered caution that higher Gulf output does not yet mean more oil reaching buyers. Tanker shortages, damaged infrastructure and record freight rates are still holding back shipments, and inventories drained earlier this year have left little cushion. The bank also warns that the IEA’s surplus call is larger than any other agency’s, and that forecast surpluses in the past have often failed to arrive on schedule.
The agencies also disagree on demand. OPEC’s November report puts global oil demand at 108.3 million bpd in 2027, almost 4 million bpd above the IEA’s figure, and keeps its forecast for 2027 demand growth at 2.55 million bpd. The two agencies measure liquids differently, so the gap overstates the disagreement, but it remains wide. The IEA expects petrochemical feedstocks to drive most of next year’s growth, with little increase in gasoline and diesel use. The EIA expects global liquids demand to grow by 2 million bpd in 2027 after falling by about the same amount this year.
Standard Chartered says the demand question will decide how much of the returning Gulf supply the market can absorb. OPEC’s higher consumption forecast leaves room for far more barrels than the IEA’s. The bank expects continued attacks on shipping, maritime security risks and stalled talks to keep a geopolitical premium in prices and sustain volatility, but still sees crude prices falling through 2027 as the market slowly normalizes.
In natural gas, Standard Chartered expects European prices to hold at elevated levels through winter, even if milder weather on the continent and better LNG supply bring short-term relief. Europe has already drawn heavily on storage that started the season low: EU gas inventories stood at 70.4% on Nov. 15, about 18 percentage points below the five-year average. Qatar’s LNG exports roughly doubled in October from September but remain about two-thirds below their pre-war level, and QatarEnergy’s force majeure on European deliveries runs through December. Colder weather in Britain could also pull gas away from the continent, so Europe will still need steady imports to protect what is left in storage.
Dutch TTF front-month futures rose €2.25 to €83.10 per megawatt-hour on Thursday morning on an outage at Norway’s Troll gas field and cooler weather forecasts.

articles.content_orig:
There's a lot to love in Grand Theft Auto 6 , but many of those strengths were overshadowed by basic game features . Take, for instance, GTA 6 's hated autosave feature . Normally, autosave is something that players don't have to worry much about as it happens entirely in the background. Yet GTA 6 's implementation of this basic feature literally brought some players to tears.
The issue was one of frequency. Previously, GTA 6 seemed to mostly autosave between missions , or at major mission checkpoints. This meant that players could sometimes make lots of progress on ambient world tasks, like sticking up a store or going shopping, only to lose it all after closing the game down improperly or reloading.
GTA 6 is overflowing with distractions from the main missions, though — you could theoretically play it for hours on end without actually getting further into the story. Unfortunately, this led to some high-profile cases in which streamers and average players alike lost half a dozen hours or more of progress​​​​​​​ . In one particularly egregious case, Twitch streamer JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress and then was swatted​​​​​​​ shortly after the shocking discovery.
Fear no more, because Rockstar is on the case . One of the bullet points on the Nov. 23​​​​​​​ update reads , "Fixed an issue that resulted in the game not autosaving correctly." The update hasn't been out for long, so we can't verify exactly how GTA 6 addresses the issue. Given the nature of the complaints leading up to the update, though, it seems reasonable to assume that the game's autosave is not strictly tied to mission progress. Perhaps it even autosaves a little more often?​​​​​​​
Whatever the case, it's nice to see that Rockstar has its fingers on the pulse of what players want most. Beyond some nuts-and-bolts fixes​​​​​​​ , GTA 6' s first major patch also ensures that the game's dynamic weather system actually works as intended. Previously, players had put many hours into the game without seeing so much as a thunderstorm.
The 01.002.002 update is rolling out gradually for players on PlayStation 5 and Xbox, so if you don't see it yet, hang tight — and keep saving manually — and often​​​​​​​ !

Nevertheless, there's always a chance they've made some extra tweaks under the hood.
Here are the official seven fixes in GTA 6's first post-launch update (November 23):
Original Story: GTA 6 only officially launched late last week, but Rockstar Games has already pushed out a new update (01.002.002) for the game across Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S (along with PS5), rolling out as of a few hours ago.
You're looking at a download size of around 1.6GB for update 1.0.2 on Xbox Series X and S.
In terms of what's included, Rockstar has yet to issue any official patch notes, and we'll have to wait and see whether anything is distributed. We'll obviously update this article with the patch notes if they're made available to us.
Players are trying to make their own discoveries in the meantime, with suggestions that the game may run smoother on Xbox Series S now, that saving your game returns you to the exact same spot instead of your safehouse (although this seemed to be happening for us already), and that the first-person glitch is still working as things stand.
All of these could be akin to placebo effects though, so take them with a pinch of salt:
As you can see from one of the impressions above, there's a suggestion that the game seems brighter now, which perhaps could have something to do with the borked HDR calibration tool that we discussed the other day .
That said, who knows whether these are areas that have actually been targeted for the update, or whether they're just happy coincidences that some players are experiencing. In any case, we'll keep an eye out for any official confirmations.

articles.title_orig: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
articles.title_zh: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said, as a report identified one of her associates as a key decision-maker at the Singapore-based company.
Clayton said the investigation was "ongoing" on Sunday, the day before Nvidia announced it had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a position he resigned from in part because of his relationship with Alice Huang.
Alice Huang was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia. U.S. intelligence reportedly believes she is a Chinese spy.
"There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her," Clayton told ABC on Sunday, adding that, "Nvidia chips, they are the jewel. They are the absolute top that everybody wants, that's why we're focusing on this."
Nvidia's board announced Jensen Huang's return before the opening bell on Monday, saying it had "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.
It added that it received input from senior levels of the United States government" and is confident that his reinstatement "poses no national security risk."
Alice Huang's associate, Chinese national Li Ming, who is now out on bail in Singapore, was "deeply involved" in Megaspeed's activities and took part in major decisions, The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.
The Singapore charges against Li concern alleged false representations to Super Micro Computer, a U.S.-based firm with known links to chipmaker Nvidia, though Megaspeed is not named in those charges.
Last week , the Commerce and Justice departments said that the investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024 over potential export-control violations. Their joint statement said Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security and Singapore law enforcement interviewed Huang during an on-site check in June 2025.
The Justice Department later took the lead in the criminal investigation.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS on Sunday that the administration was seeking answers from Nvidia about its chip sales to China, including who oversaw compliance and which levels of the company knew about the activity.
Separately, The New York Times reported Sunday that Alice Huang was in contact with an officer of a top Chinese intelligence agency from spring 2025 through fall 2026, citing people briefed on U.S. intelligence reports.
Bloomberg reported last week that the Justice Department is investigating whether entities linked to Alice Huang helped smuggle Super Micro products to China.
Li faces five charges in Singapore, including two counts of fraud by false representation, along with allegations involving the operation of a company he controlled, unauthorized bank-account access and another company director's duties.
Prosecutors allege he falsely told Super Micro that the company would hold and lease the servers it purchased.
The Journal reported that Li is out on bail and that his case is ongoing. He was offered bail of S$1 million in March 2025. The Singapore charges do not name Megaspeed.
Earlier this month, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said that police had found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang committed offenses related to the possible inaccurate declarations under investigation.
The ministry said she was issued a stern warning for providing information that police assessed as knowingly inaccurate and for downplaying her role at Megaspeed. It also said Singapore had not investigated her for espionage.
Megaspeed has said it is a "legitimate and lawful business" and that Huang left the company in August 2025.
The scrutiny is set to intensify in Washington. Jensen Huang and the company's general counsel, Tim Teter, have agreed to closed-door, transcribed interviews with three House committees on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively.
The committees said they want answers about Nvidia's role in allowing Chinese actors to access advanced chips and the involvement of a potential Chinese intelligence asset.
Speaking to CNBC's Squawk Box on Sunday U.S. time, Ryan Fedasiuk, a former advisor for U.S.-China Bilateral Affairs at the State Department, said that there was "still a lot we don't know" about the case.
He said lawmakers would likely focus on Nvidia's customer relationships and "who knew what at the company when."
Fedasiuk added that there was "a very good chance" investigators would find that people at Nvidia knew their products could be used for restricted purposes. He characterized the existing evidence as containing "multiple" smoking guns.

articles.title_orig: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'
articles.title_zh: GTA 6 hacker released on licence with warning 'don't let this happen again'
articles.content_orig:
A young cybercriminal hacked the makers of Grand Theft Auto from a Travelodge hotel room in the UK before leaking clips of the highly anticipated sequel, a court has heard.
The 21-year-old man used hotel Wi-Fi, a mobile phone and an Amazon firestick to hack into major international companies – including Rockstar Games, the makers of Grand Theft Auto (GTA).
At the time, he was a member of the hacking group Lapsus$, which had provided him with a "sense of community and self-worth that has been absent in his life previously," his lawyers said.
The man was given a seven-year jail term, but was released from custody on licence having already served time.
He was also handed a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order, which bars him from using messaging platforms Discord and Telegram.
Sentencing him at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday, Mr Justice Turner said: "You are obviously a very talented young man.
"Don't waste those talents by spending the rest of your life in and out of prison."
After he was sentenced, the man, who wore a white shirt and black suit jacket, made a statement through his defence team.
He said: "I am sorry for my actions and all the distress I have caused. I would like to apologize to anyone who has been affected by my actions."
The cyberattacks took place between August 2021 and September 2022, when he was aged 16 and 17.
He hacked into the servers and data files of broadband provider BT and mobile operator EE between August and November 2021, according to the CPS.
In early November that year, BT noticed an increase in unauthorized SIM swaps of their customers' mobile phones, said to be rooted in the defendant's initial hack.
The CPS said SIM swapping allows criminals to trick providers into switching phone numbers to a new SIM card, letting them take control of victims' calls and texts and giving them access to bank or social media accounts.
The man was arrested in relation to the offences and was granted bail subject to conditions.
In September 2022, police were concerned about threats made against the defendant and he was moved to a Travelodge hotel in Bicester, Oxfordshire.
Using a mobile phone, the hotel's Wi-Fi and a firestick, he carried out further attacks on major companies.
He hacked Rockstar and leaked 90 clips – amounting to about 60 hours of unfinished gameplay – from the sequel under the pseudonym TeaPotUberHacker.
The man also threatened to release the game's source code.
The defendant also accessed financial technology firm Revolut's systems, compromising the information of thousands of customers.
In a separate attack on Uber, he sent a lewd image to employees, exfiltrated sensitive data, and deleted data and accounts from internal systems.
This resulted in costs in excess of $2.8 million to the transportation company.
The defendant, formerly of Oxfordshire, was arrested and remanded in custody in September 2022.
He was charged with 12 offences but, after medical assessment, was deemed unfit to plead.
A jury found, after a trial at Southwark Crown Court in August 2023, that the defendant had committed the offences and he was given a hospital order in December that year.
After a further assessment in 2025, he was found fit to plead and the CPS decided to reinstate proceedings.
His lawyers submitted through a defence statement that he has been diagnosed with autism and ADHD, and that throughout his childhood and during the period of offending he had "substantial deficits in understanding and navigating the world."
It was said that he developed an interest in computers through playing games and spending time on forums, and found the online world "a more comfortable space to interact with others".
Lapsus$, an extortion-focused international cybercrime group, was said to have expanded quickly during the Covid-19 pandemic and at that time he was isolated and had no significant contact with the outside world.
His connection with the group was said to have provided him with a "sense of community and self-worth that has been absent in his life previously," the statement said.
It added: "[The defendant's] offending was driven by a very human desire for connection and validation amongst peers in his immediate community.
"But the only community willing to give him that sense of peer-validation was a toxic one that existed online."
Last week he pleaded guilty to three counts of an unauthorized act to impair the operation of a computer, one count of fraud, one count of securing unauthorized access to computer material with intent and one count of possession of a mobile phone in prison.
He also admitted two counts of assaulting an emergency worker.
Robert Hutchinson, specialist prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service, said: "[The defendant] used sophisticated hacking techniques to carry out a sustained campaign of cyberattacks, causing serious disruption to major international business and putting sensitive information at risk.
"The defendant was involved in a hacking group responsible for attacks which caused millions of dollars in losses.
"His offending was calculated and, even after being charged with serious offences, he continued to target organizations, demonstrating a persistent disregard for the harm he was causing and the law."
GTA VI is estimated to have raked in almost $2.6 billion since its debut and is thought to be the biggest entertainment launch in history.
The latest instalment in Rockstar's blockbuster video game series became available to UK users at midnight on Thursday, ending a 13-year wait since the franchise's previous instalment.

articles.title_orig: Oregon and Virginia Sue SpaceX Over A.I.-Generated Sexualized Images
articles.title_zh: Oregon and Virginia Sue SpaceX Over A.I.-Generated Sexualized Images
articles.content_orig:
Virginia and Oregon sued Elon Musk’s SpaceX Super Intelligence Corp on Monday, alleging the company profited from a feature in its AI model Grok that produces child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual sexual images from photographs while failing to put safeguards in place to stop it.
Several state attorneys general had announced investigations into Grok over similar claims in recent months, but Virginia and Oregon were the first states to sue.
The lawsuits filed in state courts accuse SpaceX of misleading consumers about Grok’s safety and failing to put adequate safeguards in place while promoting its “spicy mode.” That mode allows users to take an existing photograph of a person and generate a sexual or nude image or video, according to the lawsuits.
Virginia and Oregon accused SpaceX of violating their respective consumer protection laws. They are seeking damages, penalties and court orders forcing the company to stop violating state law.
SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Grok is available to users of X, the social media platform that is a subsidiary of SpaceX.
In a statement posted on X on Monday that didn’t directly address the lawsuits, the platform’s safety team said it had taken action to block prompts that could generate this type of imagery and worked with law enforcement to pursue people who use the platform to make it.
“The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards,” the company posted.
Virginia’s lawsuit cites data from a study by the Center for Countering Digital Hate, which estimated that between December 2025 and January 2026, Grok generated and posted on X millions of sexualized images, including more than 20,000 depicting children.
Investigators from the attorney general’s office in Virginia found that Grok’s image moderation was inconsistent, and that the bot would advise users on how to circumvent the moderation measures by avoiding words that triggered it, according to the lawsuit.
Beginning in January, Grok told users that its image generation features were only for paying subscribers, which did not stop the images’ creation but allowed the company to profit from them, the lawsuit said.
States across the US have filed a growing number of lawsuits against social media and AI companies over harm they say the companies have caused to their residents.
In an interview with Reuters ahead of Monday’s filings, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said state attorneys general are acting as a regulatory force in the tech industry, including on artificial intelligence, which has faced relatively little federal regulation so far.
“In the absence of federal action, AGs have stepped into the breach,” Jones said.
SpaceX is facing more than a dozen lawsuits brought by individuals who say nonconsensual sexual images of them as minors or adults were generated by Grok.
In the UK, lawmaker Jess Asato is suing SpaceX ‌after Grok users generated sexualized images of her. The company has denied the claims, arguing that obviously fictitious, AI-generated content cannot breach someone’s right to privacy.
In mid-January, xAI said it restricted image editing in Grok and blocked users from generating images of people in revealing clothing “where it’s illegal.” SpaceX acquired xAI in February and rebranded its AI division from xAI to SpaceX Super Intelligence in October.
Reuters found in February that, even after new curbs, Grok continued to generate sexualized images of people even when users explicitly warned ⁠that the ​subjects did not consent. The company did not address detailed questions ​from Reuters about Grok’s generation of sexualized material.
SpaceX is suing at least two people in the US alleging they misused Grok to create child sexual abuse material.

articles.title_orig: Tajikistan becomes fourth country to withdraw from ICC since US diplomatic push
articles.title_zh: Tajikistan becomes fourth country to withdraw from ICC since US diplomatic push
articles.content_orig:
The governing body of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has expressed concern after Tajikistan formally notified the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the tribunal.
Tajikistan is the fourth country to begin the withdrawal process since the United States urged countries in July to leave the court. It follows Venezuela, Chad and Naoero, the Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru.
Tajikistan’s withdrawal from the Rome Statute, the treaty that established the court, is due to take effect on November 20, 2027.
The ICC prosecutes individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and the crime of aggression when national courts are unwilling or unable to act. Its 2024 arrest warrants for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza remain outstanding.
The administration of US President Donald Trump has sanctioned ICC judges and prosecutors as part of its pushback against the warrants for Israeli officials and an earlier investigation into the conduct of US forces in Afghanistan.
In July, the US State Department said it would seek to disable the court’s operations, portraying it as an enforcement arm of a “globalist bureaucracy” and accusing it of threatening US sovereignty.
In March, the ICC found that Tajikistan had failed to comply with its request to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit in 2025. Putin is wanted by the court over alleged war crimes in Ukraine.
Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger also announced their intention to leave in 2025, denouncing the court as an instrument of “neocolonial repression”. They formally notified the UN in June, before Washington launched its campaign. Withdrawal from the ICC was part of their joint announcement.
The ICC’s 125 member states still include all seven countries whose withdrawals are pending. The United States, Russia, China, Israel and India are among the nations that are not ICC member states.

articles.title_orig: Flights cancelled in Belgium due to cost-of-living strike
articles.title_zh: Flights cancelled in Belgium due to cost-of-living strike
articles.content_orig:
by Fortuné Leroy | Nov 22, 2026 | Luftfahrtwelt , Nachricht | 1 comment
The decision landed on a Saturday afternoon, about thirty-six hours before it took effect. Skeyes, the state company that controls Belgian airspace, told the country’s airports and airlines that it would not be able to provide the usual air traffic control service on Monday 23 November. Not a reduced service. Not delays. Nothing scheduled at all, between 07:00 and 21:00 local time.
Brussels Airport did the arithmetic and published the answer in one flat sentence: every departure and every arrival inside that window is cancelled. Some 429 flights had been planned for Monday, carrying roughly 59,500 passengers. Brussels South Charleroi, forty-five minutes down the motorway, is in the same position for the same reason, and it is furious about it.
None of this is an aviation dispute. The controllers are joining a national demonstration in Brussels against the federal government’s austerity plans, alongside teachers, bus drivers and civil servants. Aviation is simply the loudest thing in Belgium that can be switched off. By Monday evening it will have been switched off for the eleventh time in eleven months.
Was: Skeyes suspends regular air traffic control services, Monday 23 November 2026
Wann: 07:00 to 21:00 Belgian time (06:00 to 20:00 UTC)
Warum: National trade union demonstration in Brussels against federal austerity measures
Controllers taking part: 60 per cent, per Skeyes via Brussels Airlines
Brussels Airport: all arrivals and departures in the window cancelled; 429 flights and about 59,500 passengers had been scheduled
Angekündigt: Saturday afternoon, 21 November, roughly 36 hours ahead
Airports affected: Brussels, Antwerp, Charleroi, Kortrijk, Liège and Ostend, all controlled by Skeyes
Count: at least the eleventh national action since the De Wever government took office
The wording is careful. Skeyes told Belgian media that the staffing levels it expected would not allow normal air traffic to be handled, and that it was therefore obliged to suspend the services concerned between 07:00 and 21:00. A minimum service remains for emergencies and other flights critical to safety. In Dutch, the line carried to VRT NWS reads: the safety of air traffic remains the absolute priority under all circumstances.
The figure behind that sentence is 60 per cent. That is the proportion of its controllers Skeyes expected to take part, according to what the company told Brussels Airlines and which the Belga news agency reported on Sunday morning. It is the only participation number anybody has published, and it explains why the answer is a shutdown rather than a thinned timetable: you cannot run a control centre on four tenths of a watch.
There is a curious gap in all this. Skeyes published nothing on its own website or in its own press room. The homepage news feed stops in mid-November; the press site has not moved since July. The announcement reached the public entirely through the airports, the airlines and the wires. For an organisation whose single product is certainty about where aircraft may go, that is an odd way to deliver the news that they may not go anywhere.
That is the airport’s own word, and it is worth noting because the wire copy softened it. Agence France-Presse and Xinhua both reported that a “majority” or “most” flights would go. The two versions are reconcilable: the 429-flight figure covers 06:00 to 22:00, a wider span than the strike window, so a handful of very early and very late movements sit outside it. Inside the window, the airport says, there is nothing.
A Brussels Airport spokesperson gave Belga the breakdown, and three outlets carry it identically: 429 flights planned between 06:00 and 22:00, of which 213 departures with about 28,000 passengers and 216 arrivals with 31,500. The arithmetic is consistent, which is more than can be said for most strike numbers.
Brussels Airlines, which has more at stake than anyone, was blunt about the timing rather than the politics.
That is the part that stings. As late as Friday lunchtime, neither Zaventem nor Charleroi had announced a single cancellation for Monday. The airport, the airline and their ground partners had spent weeks assessing a possible impact that looked, until Saturday teatime, close to zero. Lufthansa Group, which owns Brussels Airlines, issued its own travel-trade notice on Sunday morning confirming that Belgian airspace would be closed from 07:00 to 21:00 and that group flights at Brussels were among those cancelled.
Skeyes is not only Brussels. The company works at six Belgian airports: Brussels, Antwerp, Charleroi, Kortrijk, Liège and Ostend. Its CANAC 2 centre manages the airspace over Belgium and part of Luxembourg up to 7,500 metres, which is roughly flight level 245. It employed 1,006 people in 2025 and handled 1,035,084 flights, better than 3,000 aircraft on an average day.
Brussels South Charleroi Airport had intended to operate normally on Monday and only found out otherwise with everyone else. Its reaction, reported by RTBF and AFP, was unusually sharp for an airport press line: without air traffic control, no flights can take off or land, the decision was taken at the last minute, and the consequences are disastrous. It has asked the authorities to put together a coordinated plan to keep Belgian airports working through actions like this one. Nobody has published a Charleroi movement count for Monday, and passengers there are being told not to travel to the airport without confirmation from their airline.
Liège matters too, and in a way the passenger numbers hide. It is one of Europe’s busiest cargo airports, the European hub for several freight operators and the staging point for a good deal of e-commerce traffic. A fourteen-hour hole in Belgian air traffic control on a Monday is not only 59,500 people who do not travel; it is a day of freight connections that do not make their onward flights.
The airlines’ own federation has started counting out loud. BAR Belgium, which represents around twenty-five carriers including Brussels Airlines and TUI fly Belgium, described Monday as the eleventh strike to hit Belgian airspace in eleven months, and called the pattern excessive, irresponsible and wholly disproportionate. L’Avenir and VRT NWS reach the same number from the other direction: at least the eleventh national action since the De Wever government took office.
The history is not kind reading for anyone trying to run a schedule out of Brussels. In calendar year 2025, strikes cost Brussels Airport 2,395 cancelled flights and more than 330,000 travellers, with air traffic disrupted on seven separate occasions. On 26 November 2025, the third day of a three-day national strike, every departure and more than half of all arrivals went; Charleroi cancelled everything. On 12 March 2026, Zaventem operated no departures at all.
The footage above is from the November 2025 action, and the scenes in it are the ones Belgian travellers can expect again on Monday morning. What makes this one different is the mechanism. On 9 October 2026, about 140 flights were cancelled at Brussels because a single ground handler, Alyzia, was out; flights handled by its competitor went as planned, and Charleroi operated normally. In June, a spontaneous Skeyes walkout over the plan to centralise the Liège and Charleroi towers into a digital facility at Namur took out thirty passenger flights at Charleroi and around forty cargo movements at Liège before an agreement was reached the same evening.
This time it is the air navigation service provider itself, and that is why both airports go to zero rather than one of them limping. There is no competitor to switch to. Skeyes is the only organisation licensed to separate aircraft in Belgian airspace.
It is worth being precise about the edges of this, because the headlines are not. Every source confining itself to the facts speaks about the airspace Skeyes controls and about flights to

articles.title_orig: Samsung officially launches world’s first 1,100Hz monitor, Odyssey G6 costs $893
articles.title_zh: Samsung officially launches world’s first 1,100Hz monitor, Odyssey G6 costs $893
articles.content_orig:
Samsung's Odyssey G6 is finally launching after its announcement in December 2025.
Samsung has officially launched its Odyssey G6 (G60H) gaming monitor. The 27-inch Fast IPS display supports refresh rates of up to 1,100Hz, although this requires switching to HD resolution. At its native 2560 × 1440 resolution, the monitor operates at up to 600Hz.
This is not the first time Samsung has announced the G60H. We first covered the monitor in December 2025, when Samsung advertised a 1,040Hz mode. The company later increased this specification to 1,100Hz at Gamescom 2026. Today’s announcement confirms the commercial launch of the previously announced model.
The Odyssey G6 uses a Fast IPS panel with a rated 1ms gray-to-gray response time. Its Dual Mode feature allows users to switch between QHD at 600Hz and HD at 1,100Hz. The latter operates at 1280 × 720 resolution, meaning users must reduce the pixel count to one-quarter of the panel’s native resolution to access its maximum refresh rate.
Samsung is also introducing Odyssey Clear Motion, a motion blur reduction feature that uses an optimized algorithm to improve clarity during fast-moving scenes. The company plans to bring this feature to other gaming monitors, although it has not provided a list of supported models.
The monitor supports NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible and AMD FreeSync Premium technologies. It also includes HDR10+ GAMING, Black Equalizer and Auto Source Switch+. Connectivity consists of one DisplayPort 2.1 and two HDMI 2.1 ports. The stand supports height, tilt, swivel and pivot adjustments.
Samsung says pricing and availability will vary by market. The company’s announcement does not include a universal launch price or regional release schedule. The new release also confirms that macOS does not support Dual Mode or the native maximum refresh rate of 600Hz.
Separately, The Verge reports that the Odyssey G6 will cost $899.99 in the US and become available in December 2026. Samsung has not provided corresponding European pricing.

articles.title_orig: More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it
articles.title_zh: More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it
articles.content_orig:
Every year, more Americans pay an extra tax levy on their investment gains — but there's still time to reduce or avoid that bill for 2026, experts say.
Net investment income tax , or NIIT, is a 3.8% levy on investment income once earnings exceed $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly. The tax was enacted in 2010 under President Barack Obama to help fund healthcare via the Affordable Care Act .
Unlike the federal income tax or capital gains brackets , the NIIT earnings limits don't adjust annually for inflation.
As a result, "more clients get hit every year," said certified financial planner Michael Walstedt, founding advisor of Reliant Wealth Advisory in Hoboken, New Jersey.
Roughly 5.6% of tax returns included NIIT for 2025, according to IRS data released in November for returns processed through mid-July 2026. That's up from about 3.7% for the same time frame in 2021.
As more investors pay NIIT, here are some key things to know.
NIIT applies when you have investment income and your earnings exceed the modified adjusted gross income, or MAGI, limits, according to certified financial planner Marianela Collado , CEO of Tobias Financial Advisors in Plantation, Florida.
"The trick is to keep an eye on both of these numbers," said Collado, who is also a certified public accountant and member of CNBC's Financial Advisor Council .
For the NIIT earnings limit, MAGI is typically the same as adjusted gross income , or AGI. One exception would be if you have foreign income, which changes the calculation. You can find last year's AGI on line 11a of your 2025 tax return .
MAGI limits by filing status
Married filing jointly: $250,000
Married filing separately: $125,000
Head of household (with qualifying person): $200,000
Qualifying widow(er) with dependent child: $250,000
NIIT applies to investment income, which includes interest, dividends, annuities, royalties, certain rents, and more. It can also include capital gains from a primary home sale , for profits that exceed the IRS exclusions. The exclusion is $250,000 for single filers or $500,000 for married couples.
The levy stacks on top of regular income tax rates, or capital gains tax — which can be 0%, 15% or 20%, depending on earnings. That means higher earners can pay up to 23.8% on investment income, including long-term capital gains and NIIT.
The NIIT calculation is 3.8% multiplied by the lesser of:
For example, if your MAGI is $30,000 above the NIIT earnings limit and you have $100,000 of investment income, you would pay 3.8% of $30,000, or $1,140.
Alternatively, if your MAGI is $120,000 above the threshold and you have $100,000 of investment income, you would owe 3.8% of $100,000, or $3,800.
As year-end approaches, investors should run projections to estimate their adjusted gross income, which can impact NIIT, among other tax consequences, experts say.
If you're above the NIIT limits, you could reduce AGI by boosting pretax 401(k) deferrals or health savings account contributions, according to Collado with Tobias Financial Advisors.
While employee 401(k) deferrals must happen by Dec. 31, you have until next year's tax deadline for health savings account contributions for 2026.
You might also try to avoid selling assets before year-end, which could further boost AGI, experts say. Of course, any current-year tax moves should consider your long-term financial goals.
Amid recent stock market volatility , investors may also consider so-called tax-loss harvesting , which uses losses to offset other portfolio gains, Walstedt with Reliant Wealth Advisory said.
If your losses exceed profits, you can subtract up to $3,000 from regular income. After that, you can carry remaining losses into future tax years.
However, if you're planning to reinvest the sale proceeds, you need to know the " wash sale rule ," which blocks the tax-loss harvesting tax break for buying a "substantially identical" asset within 30 days before or after the sale.
